paragraphs.title: A Prayer to Guard Speech and Heart

easy.explanation: David cries unto the LORD and asks Him to hear his voice.
easy.q: To whom does David cry at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: He asks that his prayer be set before the LORD as incense.
easy.q: What does David compare his prayer to?

easy.explanation: David asks the LORD to set a watch before his mouth and keep the door of his lips.
easy.q: What does David ask the LORD to watch over?

answers: Both describe falling into a net
medium.explanation: David asks that his heart not incline to evil and that his speech be guarded.
medium.q: What connection is made between guarding the mouth and guarding the heart?

medium.explanation: “Dainties” means the pleasant things or pleasures associated with the wicked.
medium.q: In verse 4, what are the wicked men’s “dainties”?

medium.explanation: David says that being smitten and reproved by the righteous would be a kindness.
medium.q: What does David prefer to sharing in the works and dainties of the wicked?

answers: From calling on God to guarding speech and the heart
From war to building a city
challenge.explanation: David prays for help and asks that the answer be shown in disciplined speech and a faithful heart.
challenge.q: What movement occurs in this passage, from prayer to conduct?

answers: Because it corrects him and keeps him from evil
Because it gives him pleasant things
challenge.explanation: David welcomes correction because it can keep him from following the way of wickedness.
challenge.q: Why does David regard the righteous person’s reproof as a kindness?

answers: Prayer is presented before the LORD as an offering
Prayer is only made during war
Prayer is intended for wicked people
challenge.explanation: David presents prayer and lifted hands as acts of worship brought before the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the comparison of prayer to incense and the evening sacrifice suggest?

easy.explanation: The verse says that their judges are overthrown in stony places.
easy.q: What happens to the judges of the wicked, according to verse 6?

easy.explanation: Their bones are pictured as scattered at the grave’s mouth, showing extreme distress.
easy.q: How are David and his people pictured in verse 7?

easy.explanation: After their overthrow, they shall hear David’s words, which are described as sweet.
easy.q: What will the fallen judges hear?

answers: After their overthrow, they hear his words
His words cause them to receive dainties
There is no connection between the two statements
medium.explanation: Verse 6 joins their overthrow with their hearing David’s sweet words.
medium.q: What connection is made between the judges being overthrown and hearing David’s words?

medium.explanation: To be overthrown is to be brought down or defeated.

answers: A condition of brokenness and great danger
medium.explanation: Scattered bones near the grave represent severe suffering and danger.
medium.q: What does the picture of scattered bones emphasize?

answers: David presents himself as suffering rather than creating it
David does not address it at all
challenge.explanation: The passage portrays David and his people as afflicted and scattered, not as the source of the hostility.
challenge.q: What attitude toward hostility is expressed in this passage?

answers: David’s sweet words and his broken condition
challenge.explanation: Although David’s condition is pictured as broken, his words are still described as sweet.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the passage?

challenge.explanation: The grave’s mouth conveys extreme danger and closeness to death.
challenge.q: What does the image of the grave’s mouth suggest?

paragraphs.title: Refuge in God and Escape from Traps

easy.explanation: David says that his eyes are unto the LORD God.
easy.q: To whom does David turn his eyes?

easy.explanation: David declares, “in thee is my trust,” speaking to God.
easy.q: In whom does David place his trust?

easy.explanation: David asks God to keep him from the snares and gins laid by the workers of iniquity.
easy.q: From what does David ask to be kept?

answers: Keep it from hearing his words
medium.explanation: David asks God, “leave not my soul destitute,” meaning do not abandon it.
medium.q: What does David ask God not to do to his soul?

medium.explanation: A gin is a trap used to catch someone or something.

answers: That he will fall into a snare
That the wicked will fall into their nets while he escapes
medium.explanation: David asks that the wicked fall into their own nets while he escapes.
medium.q: What outcome does David hope for?

answers: Trust in God is the basis for asking Him for protection
challenge.explanation: Because David trusts in God, he looks to Him for protection from the snares of the wicked.
challenge.q: What is the connection between trusting in God and asking to be kept from traps?

answers: The wicked fall while David escapes
Incense is contrasted with the evening sacrifice
challenge.explanation: The wicked are to fall into their own nets, while David escapes.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the passage?

answers: The danger is an intentional trap set by enemies
The danger is a natural sickness
The danger comes from the righteous person’s correction
challenge.explanation: The verse describes snares and gins deliberately laid by the workers of iniquity.
challenge.q: What does the mention of snares laid by the workers of iniquity imply?
